item.title: Kopi Tubruk: The Indonesian Unfiltered Coffee — Authentic Recipe & Complete Brewing Guide
item.description: Kopi tubruk is Indonesia's unfiltered coffee: pour near-boiling water directly onto fine grounds, wait 4 minutes for the grounds to settle, drink the supernatant. Full recipe (1:13 ratio, 90–95°C water), origin, kopi joss variant, and how it differs from Turkish coffee.

item.title: Ipoh White Coffee: Authentic Malaysian Recipe, Margarine-Roasted Beans & Brewing Guide
item.description: Ipoh white coffee is a Malaysian coffee from Ipoh, Perak made from beans roasted with palm-oil margarine (no sugar or wheat) and served with sweetened condensed milk. Full origin, the unique margarine-roasting process, an authentic 3-in-1 home recipe, and how it differs from other 'white coffees'.

item.title: Kissaten: Inside Japan's Showa-Era Coffee Houses (Culture, Etiquette & How to Spot a Real One)
item.description: A kissaten (喫茶店) is a traditional Japanese coffee house — Showa-era retro decor, hand-drip or siphon coffee, and quiet hospitality. Here's the full guide: 1888 origin, jazz/pure/meikyoku subgenres, etiquette, and how kissaten differ from modern Japanese cafes.

item.title: What Is Yemeni Coffee? Origin, Qishr, Qahwa & Brewing Guide
item.description: Yemen is the birthplace of cultivated coffee. Learn authentic Yemeni coffee — Haraz beans, qahwa with cardamom and cinnamon, and qishr (caffeine-free coffee husk drink) — and how to brew it at home.

item.title: What Is Arabic Coffee (Qahwa)? How to Make It at Home
item.description: Arabic coffee (qahwa) is a spiced cardamom coffee from the Arabian Peninsula — distinct from Turkish coffee. Learn what makes it different and how to brew it at home.
